analysis.investment_thesis: MedPlus is a legitimate pharmacy retail rollout story in India's still-fragmented drug retail market, with FY2025 showing a dramatic FCF and profit inflection (FCF: INR 482 Cr, net profit up 127% YoY). However, at 51x earnings with revenue growth decelerating to just 9% in FY2025 and ROE a meagre 8.8%, the price is running well ahead of the business quality.
key_strengths: FCF inflection — FY2025 free cash flow hit INR 482 Cr vs. near-zero or negative in prior years, signalling network maturity
India pharmacy consolidation runway — organised chains still hold <20% of the INR 2L+ Cr market, giving MedPlus a long store-roll story
EBITDA compounding at 30.9% CAGR over 9 years, with operating income tripling since FY2020
key_risks: Revenue growth decelerating sharply — FY2025 top-line grew only 9% (INR 5,625→6,136 Cr), well below the 15% CAGR average; for a 51x P/E stock this is dangerous
ROE of only 8.8% — Lynch demands >12%; thin 4.75% operating margins and high lease/finance costs structurally cap return on equity
Volatile net profit history — profits swung wildly (INR 2 Cr in FY2020, INR 50 Cr in FY2023, INR 150 Cr in FY2025), making earnings quality hard to trust
red_flags: PEG ratio ~1.4–2.1 depending on growth assumption — well above Lynch's 1.0 threshold, overvalued for the actual growth being delivered
Debt growing steadily (borrowings: INR 477 Cr in FY2020 → INR 1,193 Cr in FY2025) and D/E at 0.65, above comfort zone for a thin-margin retailer
Finance costs at INR 103 Cr eating into thin margins — interest coverage still manageable but leaves no room for error
analysis.detailed_analysis:
MedPlus is a classic retail roll-out story — the kind I like in principle. India's pharmacy retail market is fragmented enough that a well-run chain can gain share for years. The 9-year EBITDA CAGR of 31% and the FY2025 FCF of INR 482 Cr tell me the mature stores are now generating real cash. Private-label pharma manufacturing is a nice added wrinkle that could eventually lift margins above the current 4.75% operating figure. The promoter holding at 40% and strong DII+FII combined ownership of 43% signal reasonable institutional conviction.

The problem is the price. At 51x trailing earnings with revenue growth slowing to 9% in FY2025, the PEG lands around 1.4–2.1x — well outside the <1.0 zone where I get excited. ROE at 8.8% is frankly sub-par; a retailer expanding with lease-heavy capex and 4.75% operating margins is not compounding equity well. The profit line has been too erratic — swinging from INR 2 Cr to INR 150 Cr over five years — for me to trust a single bumper year as the new baseline. I'd want to see two more years of 20%+ revenue growth with stable or expanding margins before paying this multiple. Right now it's a business with a good story but a stretched price tag.
